summary: This MathWorks documentation example sets up an end-to-end pick-and-place workflow for a Kinova Gen3 manipulator simulated in Gazebo and controlled from MATLAB over ROS 1. The robot scans the scene with a depth camera, builds a point-cloud-based planning scene, detects bottles and cans with ICP registration, and uses RRT path planning to move recyclable parts into two bins. The page also includes navigation and boilerplate, which were ignored.
one_line: MathWorks example of a Kinova Gen3 arm sorting recyclable parts in Gazebo using point-cloud processing, ICP detection, and RRT path planning.
key_facts: The example sets up an end-to-end pick-and-place workflow for a robotic manipulator like the Kinova Gen3.
The example identifies and recycles objects into two bins using a Kinova Gen3 manipulator.
The example uses tools from five toolboxes, including Robotics System Toolbox, ROS Toolbox, Image Processing Toolbox, and Computer Vision Toolbox.
The simulation runs in Gazebo using ROS 1, and the VM contains ROS Melodic.
The MATLAB connection to ROS is started with rosinit using port 11311.
The robot moves to scanning poses and captures point clouds with an onboard depth sensor, then merges them using pcmerge.
The merged point cloud is segmented based on Euclidean distance using pcsegdist, and the segments are encoded as collision meshes for RRT path planning.
The manipulatorRRT object plans paths from an initial to a desired joint configuration while avoiding collisions.
Trajectories are generated with trapveltraj using a trapezoidal profile and sampled every 0.1 seconds.
The functions exampleCommandDetectParts and exampleCommandClassifyParts use the pcregistericp (ICP) algorithm to identify which segmented point clouds match objects to pick.
In the sample run, the detection step reported 'Bottle detected...' and 'Can detected...'.
The gripper is controlled through the action '/my_gen3/custom_gripper_controller/gripper_cmd'.
The joint-trajectory controller is implemented in the KINOVA ROS package (ros_kortex), which uses ros_control.
The placing poses are defined for two belts at positions [0.2 0.55 0.26] and [0.2 -0.55 0.26].
